title: My working day at Delta Ducon
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a descrever a sua rotina de trabalho usando o Present Simple na forma afirmativa. Como assistente administrativo, você organiza agendas, atende ligações e cuida de documentos todos os dias — e essas são exatamente as frases que você vai usar para explicar o que faz na Delta Ducon.
intro: Every morning at Delta Ducon starts with a plan. You open your email, you check the agenda, and you get the office ready for the day.
Today we practise the Present Simple, the tense we use for routines. It helps you say what you do at work every day, from the first call to the last document you file.
introAudio: Good morning. I am your English teacher. Today we talk about routines. I open my email, I check the agenda, and I answer the phone. Let us practise your working day together.
vocab: I check the email every morning.
I organize the manager's agenda for the week.
The director has a meeting at nine.
I file each document in the right folder.
I welcome every visitor at reception.
I send the report to the ISO team.
practice: I check the ______ before the team arrives.
I update the director's ______ every Monday.
The board has a ______ in the main room at ten.
I sign each ______ and save a copy.
I greet every ______ at the front desk.
I prepare the monthly ______ for the ISO 9001 audit.
She reads the ______ and answers the client.
He brings one ______ to the reception desk.

audio.title: A day at reception
audio.text: Maria works as an administrative assistant at Delta Ducon. She arrives at eight and opens the office. She checks the email and updates the director's agenda. She answers the phone and welcomes each visitor. She files every document for the ISO 9001 system. In the afternoon, she prepares the report and sends it to the engineering team.

readAloud: I open the office at eight o'clock.
The director reads the report every day.
We answer the phone at reception.
She files the documents in the ISO folder.
The team sends the agenda by email.
fill: He ___ the report to the client. (send)
I ___ every visitor with a smile. (welcome)
They ___ the meeting room before nine. (prepare)
She ___ the files in the ISO system. (keep)
qa: What do you do every morning?
I check the email and update the agenda.
Where do you work?
I work at Delta Ducon.
Who welcomes the visitors?
I welcome the visitors at reception.
What does the director do at ten?
The director has a meeting.
How do you send the report?
I send the report by email.

a.label: I
a.placeholder: I check the email every morning.

sentences: I open the office every morning.
I check the email before the team arrives.
I update the director's agenda.
She answers the phone at reception.
He signs the documents for the client.
The board has a meeting at ten.
We prepare the report for the ISO audit.
The assistant welcomes every visitor.
grammarPoint: Present Simple afirmativo. Usamos para rotinas e fatos. Com I, you, we, they o verbo fica igual. Com he, she, it acrescentamos -s. I check the email. — Eu verifico o e-mail. She checks the email. — Ela verifica o e-mail.
deepDive: Para he, she e it, o verbo quase sempre ganha -s no final: work/works, open/opens, send/sends. Verbos terminados em -o, -ch, -sh, -ss, -x ganham -es: go/goes, watch/watches. Dica: pense 'ele, ela, isso' e não esqueça o -s.
examples: I check the email every morning.
Eu verifico o e-mail toda manhã.
We answer the phone at reception.
Nós atendemos o telefone na recepção.
Eles preparam a sala de reunião.
The team sends the agenda on Monday.
A equipe envia a agenda na segunda-feira.
mistakes: Com I o verbo fica sem -s.
Com we o verbo não leva -s.

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now describe your whole working day in English — a real skill for any professional.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você consegue descrever todo o seu dia de trabalho em inglês — uma habilidade real para qualquer profissional.

title: Questions and answers at the office
grammar: Present Simple — negativo e perguntas (don't / doesn't / do...? does...?)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a fazer perguntas e dizer o que não acontece usando don't, doesn't, do...? e does...?. Como assistente administrativo, você precisa confirmar horários, checar documentos e esclarecer pedidos da diretoria — e isso exige perguntar e negar com clareza.
intro: At Delta Ducon, an assistant asks many questions every day. Do we have the file? Does the director need the room? A good question saves time for the whole team.
Today we practise the negative and the question forms of the Present Simple. You will learn to use don't, doesn't, do and does with confidence.
introAudio: Do you have a busy office? I do. Today we learn to ask questions. Do we have the file? Does the director need the room? Let us practise together.
vocab: Do you have the schedule for tomorrow?
The folder does not have the signed contract.
Does the client need the invoice today?
We do not miss the deadline for the report.
Does the director have an appointment at three?
Do we call the client this morning?
practice: Do you have the ______ for next week?
The ______ does not have the signed document.
Does the ______ need the invoice by Friday?
We do not miss the ______ for the ISO report.
Does the director have an ______ at three?
Do we send the ______ to the finance team?
The manager does not change the ______ today.
Does the ______ have the visitor's details?

audio.title: Do we have everything?
audio.text: Pedro is an assistant at Delta Ducon. He does not start the day without a plan. Do we have the schedule? Does the director need the meeting room? He asks these questions every morning. He does not forget the deadlines, and he does not lose the documents. When a client calls, he asks: Do you need the invoice today? This way, the office does not miss anything important.

readAloud: I do not answer the phone during meetings.
The director does not work on Fridays.
Do you have the client's folder?
Does the team need the report today?
We do not miss the ISO deadline.
fill: I ___ not answer the phone during lunch.
___ you have the schedule for Monday?
___ the director need the meeting room?
He ___ not send the invoice on time.
___ she update the agenda every day?
qa: Do you work at Delta Ducon?
Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Does the director have a meeting today?
Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't.
Do we have the client's folder?
Yes, we do, it is here.
Does the team need the report now?
No, it doesn't, the deadline is Friday.
Do you answer emails in the morning?
Yes, I do, every day.

b.label: Negative
b.placeholder: The director does not work on Fridays.

sentences: I do not answer the phone during meetings.
She does not work on Fridays.
Do you have the client's folder?
Does the director need the meeting room?
We do not miss the ISO deadline.
Does the team send the invoice today?
They do not lose the documents.
Do we call the client this morning?
grammarPoint: Present Simple negativo e perguntas. Use do not (don't) com I, you, we, they e does not (doesn't) com he, she, it. Nas perguntas, comece com Do ou Does. Do you have the file? — Você tem o arquivo? She does not work today. — Ela não trabalha hoje.
deepDive: Atenção: depois de does e doesn't, o verbo principal volta à forma base, sem -s. Certo: She does not work. Errado: She does not works. O -s já está no does. O mesmo vale nas perguntas: Does he send? e não Does he sends?
examples: I do not answer calls at lunch.
Eu não atendo ligações no almoço.
You do not have the invoice.
She does not work on Fridays.
He does not use that folder.
Does the director need the room?
We do not miss the deadline.
Do they send the report today?
mistakes: Com she usamos doesn't, não don't.
Depois de does o verbo fica na base, sem -s.
Com she a pergunta começa com Does.
Depois de doesn't o verbo perde o -s.
You do not answer the phone.
A negativa precisa de do not.

celebrate.en: Excellent. Asking clear questions is one of the most valuable skills at any front desk.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Fazer perguntas claras é uma das habilidades mais valiosas em qualquer recepção.

title: Times and appointments
grammar: Preposições de tempo (at / in / on) + telling the time
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a dizer as horas e a usar as preposições de tempo at, in e on. Como assistente administrativo, você agenda reuniões, marca viagens e confirma compromissos da diretoria — e tudo isso depende de dizer o horário e a data corretamente em inglês.
intro: An assistant at Delta Ducon lives by the clock. The meeting is at nine, the flight is on Monday, and the audit is in March.
Today we learn to tell the time and to use at, in and on with times and dates. These small words keep every agenda clear and every appointment on time.
introAudio: What time is it now? The meeting is at nine. The flight is on Monday. The audit is in March. Today we learn to tell the time and to use at, in and on. Let us begin.
vocab: The meeting starts at nine o'clock.
The call is at half past ten.
The visitor arrives at a quarter to four.
We stop for lunch at noon.
The director's flight is on Tuesday.
The ISO audit is in September.
practice: The board meeting starts at nine ______.
The client call is at ______ ten.
The visitor arrives at a ______ to four.
The director's ______ to Uberlândia is on Tuesday.
The ISO ______ takes place in September.
The next ______ is booked for Monday morning.
The training ends at twelve ______ sharp.

audio.title: Planning the week
audio.text: Let me plan the director's week. On Monday, he has a meeting at nine o'clock. On Tuesday, his flight leaves at half past six in the morning. The ISO audit is in September, but we prepare the documents in August. At noon, the team stops for lunch. On Friday, the client visits at a quarter past two. I write every time in the agenda.

readAloud: The meeting is at nine o'clock.
The audit is in September.
The flight leaves on Monday.
We have lunch at noon.
The client arrives at half past two.
fill: The call is ___ half past three.
qa: What time is the meeting?
The meeting is at nine o'clock.
When is the ISO audit?
The audit is in September.
When does the flight leave?
The flight leaves on Monday morning.
What time do you have lunch?
I have lunch at noon.
When does the client arrive?
The client arrives at half past two.

a.label: The meeting is at ...
a.placeholder: The meeting is at ten o'clock.

sentences: The meeting is at nine o'clock.
The audit is in September.
The flight leaves on Monday.
We have lunch at noon.
The client arrives at half past two.
The training starts at a quarter to ten.
The report is due on Friday.
The director travels in the morning.
grammarPoint: at / in / on + horas. Use at para horários (at nine, at noon). Use on para dias e datas (on Monday, on 5 May). Use in para meses, anos e partes do dia (in September, in 1998, in the morning). The meeting is at ten. — A reunião é às dez. The audit is in September. — A auditoria é em setembro.
deepDive: Para dizer as horas: 9:00 = nine o'clock, 9:15 = a quarter past nine, 9:30 = half past nine, 9:45 = a quarter to ten. Dica de memória: at para o menor (hora), on para o meio (dia), in para o maior (mês, ano). Cuidado: dizemos in the morning, mas at night.
examples: The meeting is at nine o'clock.
A reunião é às nove horas.
The call is at half past ten.
A ligação é às dez e meia.
The director travels in the morning.
The report is due on Friday.
The visitor arrives at a quarter to four.
O visitante chega às quinze para as quatro.
O treinamento é em 12 de maio.
mistakes: The meeting is in nine o'clock.
The meeting is at nine o'clock.
Para horas usamos at, não in.
Para dias da semana usamos on.

celebrate.en: Great work. A clear time and date keep the whole company running smoothly — and now you can say them in English.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Um horário e uma data claros mantêm toda a empresa funcionando bem — e agora você sabe dizê-los em inglês.

title: How often do you do it?
grammar: Advérbios de frequência (always / usually / often / sometimes / never)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender os advérbios de frequência always, usually, often, sometimes e never. Como assistente administrativo, você tem tarefas diárias, semanais e ocasionais — e esses advérbios ajudam a explicar com que frequência você faz cada uma delas na Delta Ducon.
intro: Some tasks happen every day, some only now and then. I always check the email, I usually update the agenda, and I sometimes book a flight for the director.
Today we learn adverbs of frequency. They tell people how often you do something, and they make your routine at Delta Ducon easy to understand.
introAudio: How often do you check the email? I always check it in the morning. I usually update the agenda, and I sometimes book a flight. Today we learn adverbs of frequency. Let us start.
vocab: I always check the email first.
I usually update the agenda in the morning.
The director often travels to Uberlândia.
I sometimes book a flight for the team.
I never lose an important document.
practice: I ______ check the email before nine.
I ______ update the agenda in the morning.
The director ______ travels to the factories.
I ______ book a flight for the sales team.
My daily ______ starts at the front desk.
We ______ prepare the ISO files before an audit.
The manager ______ works from the Diadema office.

audio.title: My weekly routine
audio.text: I am an assistant at Delta Ducon, and I have a clear routine. I always arrive at eight and check the email. I usually update the director's agenda before the first meeting. The team often needs documents for the ISO audit, so I keep them ready. I sometimes book flights and hotels for visits to the factories. I never leave a client's call without an answer. This routine keeps the office calm and organized.

readAloud: I always check the email in the morning.
I usually update the agenda before nine.
The director often travels to the factories.
I sometimes book a flight for the team.
I never lose an important document.
fill: I ___ update the agenda in the morning. (90%)
I ___ book a flight for the team. (40%)
She ___ answers the phone at lunch. (40%)
qa: How often do you check the email?
I always check it in the morning.
Do you usually update the agenda?
Yes, I usually update it before nine.
How often does the director travel?
He often travels to the factories.
Do you sometimes book flights?
Yes, I sometimes book flights for the team.
Do you ever lose documents?
No, I never lose important documents.
sentences: I always check the email in the morning.
I usually update the agenda before nine.
The director often travels to the factories.
I sometimes book a flight for the team.
I never lose an important document.
We always prepare the ISO files before an audit.
The manager sometimes works from Diadema.
She often answers the phone at reception.
grammarPoint: Advérbios de frequência dizem com que frequência algo acontece: always (sempre), usually (geralmente), often (frequentemente), sometimes (às vezes), never (nunca). Eles vêm antes do verbo principal. I always check the email. — Eu sempre verifico o e-mail. She never forgets a meeting. — Ela nunca esquece uma reunião.
deepDive: A posição normal é antes do verbo principal: I usually work. Mas com o verbo to be, o advérbio vem depois: She is always ready. Atenção: never já é negativo, então não use don't junto. Certo: I never lose documents. Errado: I don't never lose documents.
examples: I always check the email first.
Eu sempre verifico o e-mail primeiro.
Eu às vezes reservo um voo.
She is always ready for the meeting.
Ela está sempre pronta para a reunião.
Eles às vezes visitam a fábrica.
mistakes: O advérbio vem antes do verbo principal.
Com to be o advérbio vem depois.
never já é negativo; não use don't junto.
He travels often to the factory.
He often travels to the factory.
often vem antes do verbo principal.
O advérbio é usually, não usual.

celebrate.en: Very good. Now you can explain your routine with precision — how often, not just what.
celebrate.pt: Muito bom. Agora você consegue explicar sua rotina com precisão — com que frequência, não apenas o quê.

title: Can you help me, please?
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a usar can e can't para falar do que você sabe fazer e para fazer e responder pedidos educados. Como assistente administrativo, você ajuda colegas, atende clientes e apoia a diretoria o tempo todo — e can é a palavra que torna cada pedido gentil e profissional.
intro: An assistant hears the word can all day. Can you send the report? Can you book a room? A polite can turns a request into a favour.
Today we learn to use can for ability and for polite requests, and can't when something is not possible. These words make you helpful and clear at Delta Ducon.
introAudio: Can you help me, please? Can you send the report? Today we learn to use can and can't. I can help you with any request. Let us practise polite English together.
vocab: Can you help me with the agenda?
I can send the report this afternoon.
Can you book a meeting room for ten?
I can print the contract for the client.
Can you transfer the call to the director?
I can arrange the flight for the trip.
practice: Can you ______ me with this document?
I can ______ the report by email today.
Can you ______ the meeting room for ten o'clock?
I can ______ the contract for the visitor.
Can you ______ the call to the director?
I can ______ the flight and the hotel for the trip.
Can you ______ the agenda to everyone, please?
I can ______ you find the right folder.

audio.title: At your service
audio.text: Good morning, this is reception. How can I help you? Yes, I can book the meeting room for ten o'clock. I can also print the contract and send it by email. Can you give me the client's name, please? Thank you. I can arrange the flight for the director, but I can't confirm the hotel today, because the office is closed. I can call them tomorrow morning.

readAloud: I can help you with the agenda.
Can you send the report, please?
I can't confirm the hotel today.
Can you book the meeting room?
I can print the contract for the client.
fill: I ___ help you with the document.
I ___ confirm the hotel today, sorry.
I ___ find the folder; it is not here.
He ___ arrange the flight this week.
qa: Can you help me with the agenda?
Yes, of course I can.
Can you send the report today?
Yes, I can send it this afternoon.
Can you book a meeting room?
Yes, I can book it for ten o'clock.
Can you confirm the hotel now?
No, I can't, the office is closed.
Can you transfer the call?
Yes, I can transfer it to the director.

a.label: Can you ...?
a.placeholder: Can you send the report, please?

b.label: I can / I can't
b.placeholder: I can help you with the agenda.

sentences: I can help you with the agenda.
Can you send the report, please?
I can't confirm the hotel today.
Can you book the meeting room?
I can print the contract for the client.
Can you transfer the call to the director?
I can arrange the flight for the trip.
She can speak English very well.
grammarPoint: can / can't. Use can para dizer o que você sabe ou consegue fazer, e para pedidos educados. Use can't (cannot) quando não é possível. Depois de can o verbo fica na forma base, sem to. I can help you. — Eu posso ajudar você. Can you send the report? — Você pode enviar o relatório?
deepDive: Depois de can nunca usamos to nem -s: Certo: She can send. Errado: She can to send / She cans send. Can you ...? é uma forma educada de pedir; para ser ainda mais gentil, acrescente please. A resposta curta é Yes, I can ou No, I can't.
examples: I can help you with the agenda.
Eu posso ajudar você com a agenda.
Can you send the report, please?
Você pode enviar o relatório, por favor?
I can't confirm the hotel today.
Eu não posso confirmar o hotel hoje.
Can you book the meeting room?
Você pode reservar a sala de reunião?
She can speak English very well.
Ela sabe falar inglês muito bem.
I can print the contract now.
Eu posso imprimir o contrato agora.
He can arrange the flight this week.
Ele pode organizar o voo esta semana.
We can't open the office on Sunday.
Nós não podemos abrir o escritório no domingo.
Can you help the visitor, please?
Você pode ajudar o visitante, por favor?
mistakes: Depois de can não usamos to.
Depois de can o verbo fica na base.
I can't to confirm the hotel.
Depois de can't também não usamos to.
Na pergunta, can vem antes do sujeito.
quick: I ___ help you with the agenda.

celebrate.en: Outstanding. Polite, capable English is the heart of great service — and you now speak it with confidence.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Um inglês educado e capaz é o coração do bom atendimento — e agora você o fala com confiança.
